title: The First Echo
logline: The grove repeats the egg a beat late — so there always seems to be a second one just out of sight.
epigraph: Repetition is not proof. It is only pressure.
description: Chapter 2 of Lore.Land: The First Echo. Boof carries the unnamed egg into the grove that answers a beat late, where pollen grains sleep and wake, and an echo is a summons, never a receipt.

content.text: By the second morning the egg was warmer than the feed-sack sling, the sling was warmer than Boof's ribs, and the maps in the town archive were still pretending none of this was a fact. She had walked downhill the way the waking berries pointed, off the edge of every charted furrow, into the dark treeline the field-hands would not name after sundown. The grove did not smell like an ordinary forest of loam and rotting leaves. It smelled of wet birch bark, crushed fern, and of something arriving twice.

She set the egg upon a flat mossy stone at the clearing's rim and watched the air around it thicken. The trunks stood in near-circles, curved like punctuation marks around an unsaid sentence. Pollen hung in the still green air in ring after concentric ring, gilded where canopy-light sliced through. A soft breath left her muzzle and came back a heartbeat later, wearing her own pitch, as if the thicket had caught a grain of sound asleep, held it in its throat, and then woke it up. The egg itself did not echo. The entire grove echoed the egg.

children.text: beyond the last honest furrow, a place the town labeled as reserve growth and the workers called the listening thicket. Every step pressed a different forgotten fragment from the leaf-mold: an old kitchen cough, a distant axe-stroke, a clerk saying
with the hollow confidence of someone who had never felt a warm shell.

content.text: Boof knew how towns worked. When a record-house is too clean, the dirt does not vanish; it drains downhill into the wild growth where no ledgers are audited. This thicket was where Boon.land dumped every phrase it refused to file.

content.text: The berries here did not shine for harvest distribution. They shone like grains under stress—bright when a phrase repeated often enough to become policy, dim when the thicket put them back to sleep. Boof recognized several of her own past silences reflected in the dark skins of the fruit. That was the grove’s first cruelty: it kept what the town preferred not to receipt.

content.text: "Follow me," said an echo that used Boof’s own pitch from years earlier—the careful, rhythmic clerk-voice she had used back when she thought order was a matter of correct filing. The path forked around an ancient hollow cedar and rejoined on the other side. Time here did not reverse; it re-litigated. In the suspended dust of the pollen rings, there was always a second egg, a breath behind the first, shivering in gold spores as if the grove were practicing a clutch it did not yet have the right to hatch.

content.text: Boof understood, pacing the mossy fork, that the grove was not a memory palace. It was a failure mode of the archive—overflow storage for stories that had been published too cleanly. Each echo offered a false fork: amplify a grievance, bury a name, promote an unverified rumor until it calcified into map legend. None of those routes would issue a receipt for the egg. The grove could repeat the heat; it could never file it.

Choosing a path was authorship. Leaving without choosing was also authorship, only quieter, and the grove charged compounding interest on quiet. Boof took the egg back into the sling. The phantom egg in the pollen dust remained where it hovered—a witness the thicket would never swear to in daylight. Downward, where the trees thinned into dry salt-breeze, older routes across the sand had begun to answer. She went to hear which of them would admit a turn.

content.text: Are you lost — or has the record run out of pretending?
He leaned out of a cedar where no door had been cut, pollen on mismatched sleeves, the trick no longer entirely a joke.

Boof did not answer with a riddle, and she opened no book. She wrote the grove’s first usable note on the air with her nose: an echo is not evidence; an echo is a summons; a summons is not a receipt. Then she trotted past him into the sand, because a summons still requires a response if anyone is to stay warm.

loreItems.description: Boof is a dog guide; echoes are old scents re-lit, not automatic proof.
The Grove of Echoes retains overflow testimony the polished archive will not receipt.
Pollen grains in the grove sleep and wake. Brightness is not policy until someone files it.
The grove repeats the egg a beat late, so there always seems to be a second one just out of sight.
An echo is a summons, not a receipt. Boof records this and continues toward the sand.
